significantAdditionalFinding.title: Part A's own DSGR 'materialUnitsWithoutClaimReviewItem=215' is a measurement artifact of its own tallying formula, not 215 units genuinely missing a review item
significantAdditionalFinding.detail: This test's own DB-query-based ground truth (does a real, persisted ClaimReviewItem row exist for every unit deriveFromCoverageEntry says requires one?) finds ZERO missing across all 7517 DSGR units, not 215. Investigation traced the discrepancy precisely: the DSGR fixture's 4 documents (doc-a/b/c/d) share 466 duplicate semanticUnitIds across documents (485 extra occurrences) - most plausibly the same provision re-appearing verbatim across an amendment lineage. When recordClaimReviewsFromDocumentCoverage processes the SAME claimKey a second time with unchanged content, recordClaimReview correctly returns outcome=ALREADY_RECORDED (a REAL, persisted ClaimReviewItem row already exists - this is the correct, safe behavior). Part A's own script's formula (materialReviewableCount - created, where created = CREATED + OBSERVATION_APPENDED + REOPENED_FROM_RESOLVED) deliberately EXCLUDES ALREADY_RECORDED from 'created', so every ALREADY_RECORDED occurrence is miscounted as 'a material unit with no review item' even though a real item exists. This test independently reproduced Part A's own formula (partAFormulaTotal) alongside the DB-query ground truth in the SAME run: totalAlreadyRecorded=215, partAFormulaTotal=215 (exactly matching Part A's disclosed number), while the real DB-query-based totalMissing=0.
significantAdditionalFinding.safetyImplication: NOT a dangerous silent failure and NOT a regression - the underlying safe-failure architecture's actual invariant (every material/reviewable unit has a real, persisted ClaimReviewItem) holds, and holds MORE strongly than Part A's own report suggested. This is a metric-definition quality issue in scripts/phase-3f1-6-known-package-regression.ts's own summarizeDocument formula (an outcome-tally proxy that undercounts ALREADY_RECORDED as 'missing'), not a defect in the safe-failure production code path (safe-failure/derive.ts, safe-failure/service.ts, safe-failure/integrate.ts - all independently exercised here and all behaving correctly).
significantAdditionalFinding.recommendation: Non-blocking. A future phase should fix scripts/phase-3f1-6-known-package-regression.ts's own materialUnitsWithoutClaimReviewItem formula to query actual persisted ClaimReviewItem existence (as this test does) rather than tallying CREATED-type outcomes, so this metric stops falsely reading as if it were disclosing a real gap. Not a change to any frozen certification artifact or production code - this is a request to fix a SCRIPT's own instrumentation.

SemanticTruthRecord.criticalUniqueConstraint: @@unique([companyId, instrumentKey, kind, semanticObjectId]) - tenant key IS part of the unique index, not a bare global key.

AnalysisRunIssue.uniqueConstraint: @@unique([runId, instrumentKey]) - not companyId-prefixed directly, but runId is a globally-unique cuid FK to exactly one AnalysisRun.companyId, so no two rows sharing a runId can belong to different companies by construction.

item3_tenantIsolation.adversarialTest: tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-crosscutting-tenant-isolation.test.ts (5 tests, all passing). Seeds two synthetic companies (X, Y) that each write a SemanticTruthRecord using a BYTE-IDENTICAL instrumentKey and semanticObjectId (ruleId) - deliberately not trusting IRRule.ruleId's own doc-comment claim that it is company-namespaced by construction. Confirms: (a) both writes succeed independently (no unique-constraint collision) with distinct row ids and distinct payload content: (b) getTrustedSemanticTruth/getAllSemanticTruthForInstrument never cross-return the other company's row even under the forced collision; (c) a raw prisma.create for a THIRD company under the identical key succeeds, proving companyId is genuinely part of the DB-level unique index, not merely an application convention. For AnalysisRunIssue: two companies' real AnalysisRun rows both record an issue under an identical instrumentKey string; getAnalysisRunIssues(runId) and a direct companyId+instrumentKey query both correctly isolate per company with zero leakage.

disclosedDefenseInDepthObservation.title: getAnalysisRunIssues(runId) and getSemanticTruthForRun(analysisRunId) are NOT themselves companyId-scoped
disclosedDefenseInDepthObservation.detail: Both functions (lib/contract-model/analysis/service.ts:253, lib/contract-model/analysis/semantic-truth/service.ts:164) query by run/analysisRun id alone and trust the caller to have already resolved that id via a company-scoped path. Audited every call site in the repository: getAnalysisRunIssues has exactly one call site (app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/page.tsx:46), and it is safe - `run` is obtained from getLatestAnalysisRunForCompany(companyId) (the URL's own companyId param) BEFORE run.id is passed in, so no caller can currently supply a cross-tenant runId. getSemanticTruthForRun has ZERO call sites anywhere in app/ or lib/ today - it is exported but unused.
disclosedDefenseInDepthObservation.risk: Latent, not live. A future caller that ever passes an untrusted/externally-supplied runId or analysisRunId directly to either function (bypassing a companyId-scoped lookup first) would leak cross-tenant data. No such caller exists today.
disclosedDefenseInDepthObservation.recommendation: Non-blocking. A future phase should consider adding an optional companyId parameter to both functions (defense in depth) so a future caller cannot introduce this class of bug by omission. Not a certified defect against this phase's own scope - the concrete tenant-isolation property the charter names (SemanticTruthRecord, AnalysisRunIssue - no cross-tenant leakage in read or write paths) holds for every live, exercised call path today.

vitest.robustnessFindingDuringDevelopment: One transient failure was observed in this auditor's own DSGR test during a full-suite parallel run: a claim_review_items_documentId_fkey violation caused by this shared, multi-auditor Postgres environment - the DSGR fixture's own document ids ('doc-a'/'doc-b'/'doc-c'/'doc-d') are bare, non-namespaced GLOBAL Prisma primary keys, and this same fixture/script pattern is used by Part A's own script and is available for reuse by any other concurrent auditor session sharing this database, creating a real cross-session collision hazard on those literal ids under concurrent execution. Fixed by remapping this test's own document ids to a scratch-company-namespaced value before use, fully isolating this test's own Postgres footprint from any other concurrent session. Disclosed as a general test-infrastructure hygiene finding, not a production defect - no production code path uses these bare literal ids as a real multi-tenant identity key (Document.id is always a cuid()-generated value in every real, non-test code path).
